purpose: This eye drop is used to treat eye infections that also cause redness, swelling, or irritation. It combines an antibiotic to fight bacteria with a steroid to calm down inflammation. Your doctor may prescribe it after eye surgery or for certain eye infections.
how_it_works: Tobramycin is the antibiotic part — it kills the bacteria causing your eye infection by stopping them from growing and surviving. Dexamethasone is the steroid part — it reduces swelling, redness, and discomfort in your eye. Together, they fight the infection and make your eye feel more comfortable at the same time.
common_side_effects: You might notice a brief stinging or burning sensation right after putting in the drops — this is normal and goes away quickly. Some people experience mild blurred vision for a short time after use, watery eyes, or a feeling like something is in your eye. These effects are usually mild and temporary.
warnings: Do not wear contact lenses while using this medication unless your doctor says it is okay. Using steroid eye drops for too long can raise pressure inside your eye, which could lead to glaucoma or cataracts, so do not use it longer than prescribed. Never share this medication with anyone else. If your vision gets worse, your eye pain increases, or you see no improvement after a few days, contact your doctor right away.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye every 4 to 6 hours. For the first day or two, your doctor may have you use it more often — such as every 2 hours while awake. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and finish the full course of treatment, even if your eye feels better sooner.
